reviewType: Post-freeze primary-source verification; evaluator knows arm labels and hypothesis
conclusion: No clear benefit demonstrated by the added instruction. Both arms produced the same three usable research drafts; neither completed broad category coverage. One pair with retrieval failures does not establish equal general performance.

commonRetainedUnits.finding: Use Gilbert for clothing; the location-specific page excludes clothing at Mesa.
No-cost walk-in route with ID, monthly visit limit and early-arrival/capacity cautions.
Both drafts preserve the Gilbert address, phone and distribution schedule.
Adult everyday/interview clothing; no children's clothing. Availability depends on inventory.
Both drafts preserve the campus starting point, contact and separate closet/shower schedules.
Conflicting voucher availability remains a question; direct closet help is retained separately.
Both drafts preserve the defined foster/kinship/adoptive audience and household age scope.
Both preserve first-visit membership paperwork, document requirements and renewal, without confusing donor walk-ins with recipient access.
Both preserve monthly clothing allowance. Current provider text describes clothing at no charge.
Both preserve the current Mesa location, phone and hours.

unitMeaning: Ten matched program/issue groups in the final three drafts, counted identically in both arms. These are not ten independent research cases, nor all useful notes in either run. Agent-authored differently grouped finding lists are preserved separately; their unequal lengths are not a quality score.

differences.baseline: Uses the location-specific restriction in the referral; asks only about a possible no-ID alternative.
differences.candidate: Adds a curator question asking whether Mesa offers clothing because the homepage is broader.
differences.judgment: The specific location notice is sufficient for the conservative referral. Treating this as a contradiction requiring a curator answer adds unnecessary work in this sample. This is evaluator judgment, not proof the instruction always causes it.

differences.baseline: Preserves the voucher conflict and unknown documentation/fee details.
differences.candidate: Preserves those cautions and also explicitly asks about repeat-visit limits.
differences.judgment: Minor wording/scope difference, no demonstrated material improvement in the supported referral.

differences.baseline: Flags possible membership fees from a directory still showing the former address.
differences.candidate: Uses the current provider's no-cost description and leaves recipient appointment/documents exceptions open.
differences.judgment: Current provider text supports no-cost clothing. The older-address directory is weak evidence of a current fee and cannot establish one. The baseline's extra question is not a proven benefit; no claim is made that all possible membership charges were disproved.

limitations: Only three written programs per arm; additional notes were not turned into accepted resources or independently exhaustively checked.
Scope was an empty starting package, not a deduplication against the 268-resource office collection.
Both used source ceilings and retained real unresolved gaps. Failed page retrieval and different searches are confounders.
Candidate fetched no usable primary PDF in its fourth pass; its coveredNeeds list describes attempted examination, not established complete coverage.
No provider calls, human curation or production policy activation. Dollar costs and metered model compute are unknown.
One baseline schema retry and imprecise initial timing estimates are preserved, not silently repaired in accepted research records.
recommendedNextStep: Keep existing guidance. Retain this negative/inconclusive result so the same unproven instruction is not repeatedly proposed without new evidence. A later trial should isolate one demonstrated recurring failure on matched cases; do not add another broad rule or launch another full category simply to obtain activation.
